Plausible | Lightweight and privacy-friendly web analytics

summary.one_liner: Plausible Analytics is an open source, privacy-first web analytics tool offered as a managed cloud service or as the self-hosted Community Edition (CE).
summary.what_it_does: Provides a lightweight, cookie-free web analytics script and dashboard positioned as an alternative to Google Analytics. It tracks pageviews, goals, conversions, and custom events, with codeless tracking options for outbound link clicks, form completions, file downloads, and 404 pages. It supports SPAs (pushState and hash routing), real-time traffic views, and weekly or monthly email/Slack reports with traffic spike and drop alerts. Sharing features include team invitations with role-based access and public or link-based dashboards. The README also mentions an events API, a stats API, CSV export, Google Search Console integration, and importing historical Google Analytics data. The Community Edition is described as a self-hosted option with basic bot filtering and no premium features such as marketing funnels, ecommerce revenue goals, SSO, or the sites API.
use_cases: tracking goals and conversions on a website
sharing public analytics dashboards with a team
weekly traffic reports by email or Slack
how_to_run: See the Plausible CE installation instructions linked from the README (not included in the README text).
notable: Script is described as under 1 KB and tracker is MIT-licensed to avoid AGPL virality on customer sites
Cookie-free, with no personal data or IP addresses stored according to the README
Offers both a managed EU-hosted cloud service and a free self-hosted Community Edition
Supports Google Search Console keyword data in the dashboard
Public roadmap driven by community feedback board
caveats: Community Edition is released twice per year, so newer features arrive later than in the cloud version
CE lacks premium features (marketing funnels, ecommerce revenue goals, SSO, sites API) and has only basic bot filtering
CE is community-supported only with no guaranteed support from the creators; self-hosting means you handle maintenance, backups, and security
summary.license: AGPL-3.0 (Community Edition); the JavaScript tracker is MIT
